stories.summary: Flexmls Scout is an AI assistant built directly into Flexmls, the listing system FBS sells to MLSs — the shared listing databases agents use — about 160 MLS customers, per the spring MCP launch. MCP is a standard plug that lets an AI tool pull data. Agents ask in plain language — "show me three-bedroom homes that sold in the last six months" — and Scout searches listings, pulls market stats, checks the agent's own listings, contacts and production, helps start a CMA (a comparative market analysis — the pricing report an agent shows a seller), and answers questions about MLS rules and Flexmls itself. It runs on desktop and mobile, and it is sold to MLSs as an enterprise add-on, not to individual agents. The key part: Scout only shows each user what their own login is allowed to see, the MLS keeps control of how its data is used, and FBS says MLS data is not kept or used to train the models. That is the exact shape Jessica's pitch needs — governed AI on real MLS data, with the permission built in rather than bolted on. For the product question: the MLS platform vendors are now shipping the assistant layer themselves, so the open move is not "another assistant" but what sits on top of it — the workflow the assistant can't do (the showing, the negotiation, the client relationship) or the data it can't reach (public records, off-MLS inventory). Flag: vendor announcement via trade press; no independent test of answer quality, and FBS's own docs warn AI readings can be wrong — check numbers against Flexmls before they go to a client. Note the lineage: FBS shipped the Flexmls MCP server in April (connect your own Claude/ChatGPT to MLS data); Scout is the same data, now with FBS's own assistant on top.
stories.title: Flexmls Scout: the listing system ships its own AI assistant

stories.summary: Pitching Coach, from Mojo Dialing Solutions (maker of the Mojo Dialer prospecting platform), is an AI role-play tool that lets agents practice prospecting conversations out loud and get a score after every practice call. It is in beta now for every Mojo Real Estate account, inside the Mojo web app (computer + microphone), opened from the Training section or the AI Tools page. The AI-coaching layer for agents is still thin — most agent AI writes, answers, or schedules; almost none trains the agent. A scored practice call is a different product shape: it sells skill, not output, and it plugs into the daily prospecting habit (Mojo's dialer) rather than asking for a new one. Watch whether the scoring is any good — vendor release, no independent test — but the category is open: the solo agent's practice partner, priced as training rather than software. Flag: vendor release only; no pricing, no accuracy or adoption figures.
stories.title: Mojo's Pitching Coach scores your cold-call practice

stories.summary: CoStar Group is buying Vexcel, an aerial imagery company that flies its own planes and builds its own UltraCam cameras, for about $730 million in cash. The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. CoStar already owns the biggest commercial-property database; now it owns the imagery supply chain that feeds it. For anyone building a product on listing or property data, the lesson is the same as the MLS story: the valuable layer is the data you control, not the app on top. Aerial imagery is becoming a first-class property-data input (roof condition, lot, neighborhood context) — and it is now inside one company's walls. Flag: trade-press roundup of a company announcement; price and close date are as announced.
stories.title: CoStar buys aerial-imagery firm Vexcel for $730M

stories.summary: Coffee & Contracts — a social-media marketing platform used by more than 6,400 real-estate agents, per the company — relaunched as an all-in-one social-media operating system for agents. The headline addition is Beans, an AI strategist trained on the company's method: it helps each agent decide what to post, checks in on its own with ideas and reports, and helps turn followers into leads. The relaunch also adds landing pages and lead capture; Instagram post scheduling is promised in the next few weeks. Current members keep their price; new members pay $74/month if they join by Nov 24. The agent-marketing stack is consolidating the same way the brokerage stack did (briefings #22–#24): one system that plans the post, publishes it, and catches the lead, instead of three separate tools. The "AI strategist that checks in on its own" is the interesting mechanic — proactive, not on-demand — and it is the same shape as the brokerage AI teammate, pointed at social instead of transactions. Flag: vendor claims (6,400 agents, Beans' capabilities) unverified; relaunch coverage only, no independent review.
stories.title: Coffee & Contracts adds Beans, an AI strategist that checks in on its own

one_line: The compliance layer for AI-altered listing photos — deadline Jan 1, 2027.

openings.text: California's rental-ad disclosure law (AB 2025) and Wisconsin's advertising rule (2025 Act 69) both take effect Jan 1, 2027, and California's sale-ad law (AB 723) has been in effect since Jan 1, 2026 — altered photos must be labeled and shown next to the original. Almost nobody keeps the original photography, and Metro MLS in Wisconsin is already fining $10/day for unlabeled altered primary photos. The open product is the boring, necessary one: a tool that archives the unedited original alongside every edited final, stamps the watermark, writes the disclosure, and files both versions where the MLS — the shared listing database agents use — and the law can see them. It is a deadline-driven purchase, not a nice-to-have — and it is the same "originals are an asset" logic as the Gems/plugin migration story in the research briefing: the thing you didn't keep is the thing the rule now asks for.
openings.title: The compliance layer for AI-altered listing photos — deadline Jan 1, 2027

watch.title: Tuccori / NAR buyer settlement — still no outcome, 7 days after the hearing

watch.text: California AB 2025 (rental ads, altered or fully AI-generated images) and Wisconsin 2025 Act 69 (licensee advertising altered with technology, including AI, in a way that creates a false or misleading impression) both take effect Jan 1, 2027. California AB 723 (sale ads) has been in effect since Jan 1, 2026. Metro MLS (Wisconsin) has enforced its photo rules since Sept 1 — $10/day for an unlabeled altered primary photo, $10 for a missing watermark, original uploaded immediately before the altered version. Bills pending in New York, New Jersey, and Washington, D.C. — not law yet. Source: aiandrealtors.com state-law guide (reviewed Nov 2) + NanaStack #013 (Nov 2, summarizing WGAN's Oct 30 roundup). The "thousands of communities need new photography" and lawsuit predictions are interviewee estimates, not verified data.
watch.title: AI photo disclosure — hard deadline Jan 1, 2027
